To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a GaN-based microcavity light-emitting diode (MC LED) with a buried aluminum nitride (AlN) current aperture has been demonstrated.
a high-Q MCLED can be realized with the buried AlN current blocking layer.
the GaN-based MCLEDS with buried AlN aperture exhibit a very high Q value of 846 at an operating current of 5mA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication of a GaN-based MC-LEDs with high-Q and high-efficiency.
the development of high-Q MCLEDs with buried AlN layers for the realization of a new class of high-brightness light source.
the fabrication and the optical properties of a GaN-based MC LED with a buried AlGaN current aperture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GaN-based MC LED with the buried AlN current confinement layer has a high-Q factor and narrow emission spectrum, which is suitable for high-resolution optical communication applications.
the AlN current aperture can effectively improve the current injection efficiency of the MCLED, resulting in a high-Q MCLED.
we have demonstrated a high-Q MCLED with a thin buried AlN current blocking layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the buried AlN current blocking layer can be applied in the GaN-based MCs for high-Q light emission.
the AlN layer is a very promising material for the application of GaN-based MCLEDS.
the buried AlN layer is an effective current blocking layer and optical confinement layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the buried AlN current confinement layer can be applied to other types of GaN-based MCLEDS with a DBR mirror.
the AlN current blocking layer can effectively reduce the current crowding effect and improve the current injection efficiency.
a buried AlN layer can be used as a current aperture in GaN-based MCLEDS.
